decision_table.name: Determine_LA_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file Louisiana state corporate tax return. Checks for physical presence or economic nexus.

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in Louisiana (office, employees, property)

condition.name: has_economic_nexus
condition.comment: Meets Louisiana economic nexus threshold ($100,000 gross receipts)

actions.action: // Physical nexus established - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
Louisiana filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in state).
A corporation has physical presence nexus in LA if it has: - An office, store, warehouse, or other place of business in LA - Employees working in LA - Tangible personal property located in LA - Real property located in LA
Reference: Louisiana Revised Statute 47:287.1 et seq. Reference: LA Form CIFT-620 Instructions

actions.action: // Economic nexus established per Wayfair - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
Louisiana filing required due to economic nexus (post-Wayfair).
Economic nexus threshold: $100,000 gross receipts from Louisiana customers.
Louisiana eliminated the 200-transaction threshold in August 2023, simplifying economic nexus to focus solely on dollar amounts.
Following South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018), Louisiana requires filing if a corporation exceeds the economic nexus threshold, even without physical presence.
Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018) Reference: Louisiana Department of Revenue Economic Nexus Guidance Reference: Louisiana Revised Statute 47:301(4)(k) (Economic nexus provisions)

No Louisiana nexus - no filing requirement.
Corporation does not meet physical presence or economic nexus thresholds. Any estimated payments would be refunded.
Reference: Louisiana Revised Statute 47:287.1 (Nexus requirements)

decision_table.name: Calculate_LA_Income_Adjustments
decision_table.description: Calculate Louisiana state-specific additions and subtractions to federal taxable income. Includes 2025 tax reform changes: $20,000 standard deduction and qualified property expensing.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to calculate adjustments

rule.policy:
Louisiana state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income.
LOUISIANA ADDITIONS to federal taxable income include: - Interest income from U.S. government obligations (exempt federally, taxable to LA) - State income tax refunds previously deducted federally - Expenses related to exempt income
LOUISIANA SUBTRACTIONS from federal taxable income include: - $20,000 STANDARD DEDUCTION (NEW for 2025 tax reform) - Interest on Louisiana state and municipal bonds - Louisiana net operating loss deduction (subject to LA limitations) - Qualified property immediate expensing (NEW 2025 option: costs of qualified property, qualified improvement property, and R&E expenditures may be immediately deducted if placed in service on or after January 1, 2025)
HISTORICAL NOTE: Louisiana previously allowed deduction of federal income taxes paid (unique feature among states), but this was ELIMINATED in the 2025 tax reform. The new $20,000 standard deduction partially replaces this benefit.
Reference: LA Form CIFT-620 Schedule C (Additions) Reference: LA Form CIFT-620 Schedule D (Deductions) Reference: Louisiana Revised Statute 47:287.73 (Standard deduction) Reference: Louisiana Revised Statute 47:287.85 (Adjustments to federal taxable income) Reference: Grant Thornton Tax Alert (Dec 2024) - LA Tax Reform

No nexus - no state adjustments calculated.
Corporation does not have Louisiana nexus, so no income adjustments are needed.

decision_table.name: Calculate_LA_State_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate Louisiana state corporate income tax. Applies LA 5.5% flat rate to apportioned and adjusted taxable income. NEW 2025: Flat rate replaced graduated rates, includes $20,000 standard deduction.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe tax

rule.policy:
Louisiana state corporate income tax calculation (2025 TAX REFORM):
1. Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28] 2. Apportioned to Louisiana: × [LA single-sales apportionment percentage] 3. Louisiana additions: + [Federal interest, state tax refunds, etc.] 4. Louisiana subtractions: - [$20,000 standard deduction, LA municipal interest, qualified property expensing, LA NOL, etc.] 5. Louisiana taxable income: = [Adjusted income] 6. Louisiana tax rate: × 5.5% (NEW FLAT RATE for 2025+) 7. Louisiana income tax: = [Tax before credits] 8. Louisiana credits: - [Limited credits remaining after 2025 reform] 9. Louisiana tax liability: = [Final tax]
Louisiana uses single-sales factor apportionment (100% sales factor).
MAJOR 2025 TAX REFORM: - PREVIOUS: Graduated rates of 3.5% / 5.5% / 7.5% on income brackets - NEW 2025: Flat 5.5% rate on all taxable income - ADDED: $20,000 corporate standard deduction - ELIMINATED: Federal income tax deduction (historically unique LA feature) - ELIMINATED: Many tax credits (jobs creation, solar energy, educational contributions) - FUTURE: Corporation franchise tax repealed for periods beginning January 1, 2026
Louisiana tax rate history: - 2025+: 5.5% flat rate (new reform) - Prior to 2025: 3.5% on first $50K, 5.5% on $50K-$150K, 7.5% over $150K - Historical unique feature: Federal income tax deduction (eliminated in 2025 reform)
Reference: LA Form CIFT-620 (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: Louisiana Revised Statute 47:287.12 (Tax rate: 5.5% flat) Reference: Louisiana Revised Statute 47:287.73 ($20,000 standard deduction) Reference: Louisiana Revised Statute 47:287.94 (Single-sales apportionment) Reference: Louisiana Department of Revenue Tax Reform Bulletin (2024) Reference: Grant Thornton Tax Alert (Dec 20, 2024) - LA Tax Reform

No Louisiana nexus - no tax liability.
Corporation does not have physical presence or economic nexus in Louisiana. Any estimated payments are refunded.
Reference: Louisiana Revised Statute 47:287.1 (Nexus requirements)

No Louisiana taxable income - no tax liability.
Corporation has Louisiana nexus but no positive taxable income after apportionment and adjustments (including $20,000 standard deduction). Any estimated payments are refunded.
Louisiana net operating loss (NOL) rules may apply: - Louisiana allows NOL carryforward - NOL deduction subject to Louisiana limitations - Carryforward period follows federal rules with Louisiana modifications
Reference: LA Form CIFT-620 (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: Louisiana Revised Statute 47:287.86 (Net operating loss deduction)
